data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Decentralized networks are more resilient specifically because they avoid the 'Standardization Trap', where the pursuit of efficiency creates systemic fragility.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The 'messiness' of the decentralized network creates so many individual failure points that the aggregate availability drops below that of a standardized centralized service.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The failure is caused by a shared standard (e.g., an RFC) that all 'diverse' services must implement to communicate.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In large services, the drive for operational efficiency leads to uniform deployment pipelines, identical monitoring thresholds, and synchronized update cycles. This standardization removes the 'buffer' of diversity. A decentralized network, by being 'inefficient' and 'messy' (diverse versions, inconsistent patching), prevents the simultaneous activation of a failure trigger. The resilience is a direct byproduct of the lack of optimization.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
